hero.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to receive 2026 All-America City Award
hero.teaser: Riviera Beach was named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League and was the only Florida city selected for the honor this year.
hero.body:
Riviera Beach has earned a prestigious national recognition as one of just 10 U.S. communities selected for the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League. The city stands alone as Florida's sole recipient of this honor. The award celebrates communities where residents, local government, businesses and organizations unite to address local problems and produce meaningful change. City leaders announced the achievement at the National Civic League conference in Denver, where they presented Riviera Beach's approach to building community engagement.

Mayor Douglas Lawson expressed pride in the honor, calling Riviera Beach "one of the biggest, brightest, shining stars." He credited the award to the city's long-term revitalization efforts aimed at improving residents' quality of life. "They're seeing the changes; they're seeing the revitalization and the reimagining of Riviera Beach that we set out so many years to do," Lawson said. City leaders emphasize that the recognition reflects sustained work to strengthen civic health, build trust between residents and government, and give community members a genuine voice in shaping the city's future.

Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson attributed the award to residents themselves. "This award is a tribute to the heart and determination of our residents," Miller-Anderson said. "Every event we host, every project we complete, and every challenge we overcome happens because our community shows up for one another." She noted that the designation reinforces the city's positive momentum and community pride. According to city officials, the award demonstrates that collaboration drives results and shows the nation that residents remain deeply involved in directing their community's future.

The application showcased several civic programs, including the Riviera Beach Youth Council, which engages high school students in civic leadership and advocacy, the Citizens Leadership Academy with a 98 percent completion rate, and the Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program, which offers mini-grants for critical home repairs to longtime homeowners. Miller-Anderson emphasized the broader commitment behind these initiatives. "We're doing a lot of innovative things to make sure that our community is able to say that they are part of what's happening here in the city," she said. The All-America City Award, presented annually since 1949, ranks among the nation's most respected civic honors. City leaders say the designation celebrates progress and positions Riviera Beach for future opportunities and continued development. Other 2026 award winners include communities in Massachusetts, Tennessee, Texas, Alabama, North Carolina, Virginia, South Carolina, and Oregon.

cards.headline: DeSantis allies accuse Lieutenant Governor's wife of running anonymous accounts attacking Governor
cards.teaser: Multiple social media accounts were deactivated Friday after prominent veterans of Governor Ron DeSantis' communications team alleged the accounts were operated.
cards.body:
Multiple X accounts were deactivated after allegations from prominent veterans of Governor Ron DeSantis' communications team that they were operated by Layla Collins, wife of Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins. Christina Pushaw, a communications specialist in the Governor's Office, and Jeremy Redfern, Deputy Chief of Staff to Attorney General James Uthmeier, both pointed to online research tying the accounts to the Second Lady. Pushaw shared information from Promota CEO Robert Salvador showing that the account @FSUdude01670 appeared connected to a phone number and email similar to known contact information for Layla Collins. Florida Politics obtained screenshots verifying this through two-factor authentication, displaying an access attempt that triggered a message to a partially starred email address and a phone number with only the last digits visible.

Pushaw also identified a second account, @bobnamy1, that she said appeared tied to Layla Collins, stating its content consisted entirely of posts promoting Jay Collins and attacking people who did not endorse him, including the Governor. Redfern posted that the FSUDude account was tied directly to Layla Collins' personal cell phone number. Both accounts were deactivated after the public criticism. Florida Politics requested comments from Jay and Layla Collins. Both Pushaw and Redfern previously served as Press Secretaries for DeSantis. Redfern now works for Uthmeier, who has endorsed U.S. Representative Byron Donalds for Governor.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board fights judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk Facebook post
cards.teaser: The Martin County School Board filed a court challenge Thursday against a judge's recommendation to reinstate a Spectrum Academy teacher suspended last year for.
cards.body:
The Martin County School Board is pushing back against a judge's recommendation to reinstate a teacher suspended last year following controversial social media comments about Charlie Kirk. Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009, sparked controversy with his comments, which labeled Kirk as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi. In a Thursday court filing, the school board argued Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone erred in recommending Theobald get his job back, saying numerous findings are not based upon competent substantial evidence. The board's attorney claims Theobald's Facebook post about Kirk was a serious offense and removing him was appropriate.

In an order issued last month, Livingstone cited a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling that said disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds, on personal equipment, with no student involvement, violated the teacher's First Amendment rights. The judge also recommended Theobald be awarded back pay and benefits. According to an investigation report, Theobald admitted writing the comments about Kirk but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page within a discussion among personal acquaintances and were not intended for public view.

cards.headline: Martin County maritime teams prepare for hundreds of Fourth of July boaters
cards.teaser: Martin County Maritime Response Unit will have two boats with medics on standby in the north and south parts of the county as hundreds of boaters celebrate the holiday weekend.
cards.body:
Hundreds of boaters are expected on Florida waterways this Fourth of July weekend. Lt. Brett Harry with Martin County Maritime Response Unit said his team is preparing for the holiday rush with two boats staffed with medics positioned in the north and south areas of Martin County.

Harry said the medics are ready to respond to any medical situation, from minor injuries like a stubbed toe to serious emergencies including cardiac events and potential spinal injuries. Boaters Brendan and Ashley Shannon, who launched from Sandsprit Park in Martin County on Friday with their young daughter and puppy, prioritize safety on the water. Harry urged all boaters to keep their eyes on the water, designate a driver and bring life vests, whistles and flotation devices. "Just have fun and be safe," Harry said about the holiday weekend.

cards.headline: St. Petersburg selects $8.1 billion vision to redevelop Tropicana Field site
cards.teaser: Mayor Ken Welch chose a proposal led by Blake Investment Partners and Related Group to transform acres of stadium parking and public land into a mixed-use district with housing, hotels, cultural institutions and a 13-acre central park.
cards.body:
St. Petersburg Mayor Ken Welch has chosen The Burg Bid as the city's preferred proposal for transforming the Tropicana Field site and surrounding Historic Gas Plant District. The plan, led by Blake Investment Partners and Related Group, proposes an $8.1 billion mixed-use development that would replace the previous stadium-centered approach with a district organized around Samuel Davis Park, a 13-acre civic and cultural hub.

The development team would purchase 58 acres of city-owned land for $275 million, with the full land package valued at $405 million when including $130 million in land the city would retain. A $20 million deposit would be required when a purchase and sale agreement is finalized. Unlike earlier redevelopment plans centered on constructing a new baseball stadium, The Burg Bid proposal emphasizes cultural institutions and public space. Samuel Davis Park would anchor the district and include The Woodson African American Museum of Florida, a planned Museum of Public Art, a Discovery Center, event lawns, a playground, a splash pad, and a concert lawn. The park represents part of 18.5 acres of total public park space planned for the site. Blake Investment Partners CEO Thompson Whitney Blake described the project as resting "on respect for the community that once existed here, informing and educating the future generations."

The proposal emphasizes reconnecting with the Historic Gas Plant neighborhood, a predominantly Black community demolished decades ago for the stadium. The plan would preserve the original gas tank footprint within Samuel Davis Park and create a pedestrian corridor called the Legacy Link connecting City Hall with the Manhattan Casino and the Deuces District. Nine planned bridges over Booker Creek reference nine bridges that historically crossed the Gas Plant area, while restoration efforts would transform the creek from a drainage ditch back into a central natural feature with walking paths and community parks.

The development would deliver 3,600 income-restricted housing units over 15 years, with 1,800 units within the Historic Gas Plant District and 1,800 on complementary sites elsewhere in St. Petersburg. The plan includes homeownership opportunities at discounts to market value through partnership with affordable housing developer Blue Sky Communities. The project would be completed in three phases of approximately five years each, with early development beginning outside the stadium footprint before demolition. Phase 1 would establish cultural anchors and the Collaboratorium, a workforce training and small-business center. Phase 2 would develop mixed-income neighborhoods and strengthen connections to surrounding districts. Phase 3 would complete the project with a 4,000 to 5,000-seat Resilience Event Center, a Discovery Center, and a surf wave attraction. The team's lease with the city ends after the 2028 season.

cards.headline: Juno Beach residents demand fence replacement at JB-7 beach access as town faces thousands in costs
cards.teaser: A missing fence at the JB-7 public beach walkway in Juno Beach has sparked conflict between Colony Condos residents and beachgoers who are cutting through private property. The town removed the old fence in 2023 for safety reasons.
cards.body:
A dispute over a missing fence at a public beach access point in Juno Beach is creating friction between condo residents and summer beachgoers, with replacement costs potentially reaching six figures for the town. Residents at the Colony Condos say that since the town removed the old fence in 2023 for safety reasons, people using the JB-7 public walkway have been cutting through their private property to reach the beach. Currently, only bushes separate the public access path from the private land, making it easy for visitors to cross over.

Lori Hill, a Colony resident, explained that the problem intensifies during summer months. "Lots of cars that just come at random, and then they just park on the spots there," Hill said. "Bushes are pushed back that they cut through those with their coolers and their fishing rods and lawn chairs and everything, and then they just park there all day." Residents initially tried confronting trespassers to inform them about the private property boundary, but Hill said those interactions often turned hostile. Now residents call police to handle the situation when unauthorized parking and trespassing occur.

Not all community members agree on the severity of the issue. Michael House, a beachgoer who walks to JB-7 from a public parking lot nearby, disputed the residents' characterization of the problem. "There's plenty of free parking. If they're damaging property and you know littering and stuff like that might be a different issue," House said. "I have never noticed anyone hopping the fence or the shrubs or anything like that." The matter reached the Juno Beach Town Council at a recent meeting, where officials clarified that the town is not obligated to install a fence. Vice Mayor Pro Tem DD Halpern suggested exploring more affordable options rather than a full replacement. "I understand fencing is expensive, but I'd like to see maybe we can help them with a lower-cost fence or some combination of split rail and shrubs," Halpern said.

Hill expressed hope that town leadership would reconsider the fence removal. "We're really hoping that the town will get back on board and just put it back up, so that we can have our landscaping and our private parking," Hill said. The council agreed to include the fence question in budget discussions scheduled for July 15, when officials will determine whether to allocate funds for a replacement or pursue alternative solutions to address the boundary issue.

cards.headline: Breast cancer patient's insurance denies reconstruction surgery hours before procedure
cards.teaser: Beth Clark, 48, had her breast reconstruction surgery denied by Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield less than 24 hours before it was scheduled. The insurer said the GalaFlex mesh procedure is still considered investigational.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed three months ago with invasive ductal carcinoma, the most common type of breast cancer. She underwent a full double bilateral mastectomy and scheduled reconstruction surgery using GalaFlex, a synthetic surgical mesh. Less than 24 hours before the procedure, her insurance company, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, denied coverage, stating the surgery was still considered "investigational" with "no or not enough proof it improves health." GalaFlex is approved by the FDA for some uses in the body but not for breast reconstruction, making it an off-label, investigational treatment. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA stated its "efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined."

Clark's surgeon, Dr. Alicia Billington, who uses GalaFlex on most of her breast reconstruction patients, says the product gives her patients the least amount of complications compared to other options. Despite the denial, Clark received her reconstruction surgery with the GalaFlex mesh a little more than a week ago after Billington found a mechanism to make it happen. Anthem responded by stating it regularly reviews coverage policies to ensure they are based on medical evidence and aligned with treatment standards, but without FDA approval, the mesh does not currently meet coverage requirements. Last year, Cigna became the first and only major insurer to start approving GalaFlex for breast reconstruction following investigative reporting. Clark and Billington continue fighting the denial.

cards.headline: Boca Raton Community High School band to march in National Independence Day Parade
cards.teaser: The Boca Raton Community High School band earned a spot in Washington, D.C.'s National Independence Day Parade, representing the entire state of Florida. The students will march on July 4 at 10:30 a.m.
cards.body:
The Boca Raton Community High School band has earned a spot in Washington, D.C.'s National Independence Day Parade, representing Florida on July 4 at 10:30 a.m. The students will march a full mile along the National Mall, from Constitution Avenue to Independence Avenue. Only bands nominated by state officials receive invitations to this prestigious event.

Junior Lola Cabezas acknowledged the pressure of performing for millions of viewers, saying "There are millions, if not billions, of people watching. It's a lot of pressure, but I think we'll be able to rise to the occasion." Senior Stephin Restivo emphasized the team's focus on execution, stating the band is "focusing on the marching, the timing of everything" so "everyone will be able to see what the Boca High band is capable of." Band Director Jenn Girdlestone expressed confidence in her students, saying she has "full confidence in our students that they'll put their best foot forward, literally, and we'll rise to the occasion and represent our country well." Senior Lily Schaffer called the opportunity amazing, noting it "shows how much we've grown and showcases what we do here." The parade will be streamed live on YouTube for remote viewers.

cards.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs up 4% this year as inflation hits holiday staples
cards.teaser: A Fourth of July cookout for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from last year, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey. Ground beef, buns and strawberries saw the biggest price increases.
cards.body:
According to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey, a holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago. The survey attributes the increase to inflation, with ground beef prices up 5.5% and buns up 7.7%. Strawberries have been hit particularly hard by a Florida frost, rising 12.4%, while ice cream prices are up 5.3%.

Not all cookout staples have increased in cost. Potato prices are down this year, offering savings for those planning potato chips and salads. Corn prices have fluctuated, though locally grown corn from the Glades can provide the best value. Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch recommends shopping strategically by comparing prices across stores to find the best deals for items on your grocery list. She emphasizes that families should focus on cutting down food waste, which begins with creating a meal plan.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County schools earn third straight A rating from state
cards.teaser: The School District of Palm Beach County received an A rating from the state for the third year in a row. The district also achieved a record 93.5% graduation rate.
cards.body:
The School District of Palm Beach County received an "A" rating from the Florida Department of Education for the third consecutive year, reflecting strong student performance across all grade levels. This year, 143 district-operated schools, or 84%, earned "A" or "B" ratings, up from 120 schools the previous year. The district achieved a record-setting 93.5% graduation rate, with 86% of seniors participating in college-level coursework through Advanced Placement, International Baccalaureate, Cambridge Advanced International Certificate of Education, or Dual Enrollment courses. Additionally, 144 recent graduates earned an associate degree alongside their high school diploma. Superintendent Mike Burke stated that the rating reflects the district's commitment to academic success and credited the collective effort of students, teachers, school leaders, support staff, families, and community partners.

One of the district's most significant achievements came from S.D. Spady Elementary School in Delray Beach, which jumped from a "C" rating to an "A" rating this year. Principal Rona Tata, who has served in that role for 15 years, led the turnaround by modifying the school's early childhood curriculum program, which serves students starting at age 3 and combines with kindergarten. Spady Elementary was one of four district schools to improve from a "C" to an "A" rating, joining Dwight D. Eisenhower K-8, Glade View Elementary, and West Gate Elementary.

hero.headline: Hobe Sound woman dies in home fire days before her birthday
hero.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, died Monday in a fire at her Hobe Sound home. Friends launched a fundraiser to help her fiance Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed their belongings.
hero.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, died Monday after a fire broke out inside her Hobe Sound home where she lived with her fiancé Mark. Authorities discovered her body at the scene. The sheriff's office is investigating the blaze, with preliminary findings suggesting an electrical issue may have caused the fire. The investigation remains ongoing as officials work to determine the exact cause.

Mark learned of the tragedy and reached out to those closest to him to share the devastating news. Nina Fenn, who had been friends with White for eight years, received a phone call from Mark informing her that White had died in the fire. The loss struck the community hard, prompting friends to launch a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild his life. "It's completely a state of devastation," Fenn said. The flames consumed many of the couple's belongings, leaving them with significant material losses alongside their emotional pain.

Fenn spoke about who White was to those who knew her. "Misty was a Christian woman. She loved gardening and plants. She plays the piano," Fenn said. "She was always the first to lend a hand. She loves kids; she loves her kids. She loves people." White's generosity and warmth defined her relationships, and Fenn reflected on how she wants her friend to be remembered. "She's always been a good soul to me. She'll always be in our hearts," Fenn said. The depth of White's character became even more apparent as friends gathered to support Mark during this crisis.

The timing of White's death added profound sadness for everyone who cared about her. White's birthday was the Fourth of July, meaning she died just days before what should have been a celebration of her life. The tragedy compounded grief Mark was already carrying. "Mark lost his one and only child, Jacob, and lost him tragically," Fenn explained. "So, I just am trying whatever I can to support him." Fenn's commitment to standing by Mark reflected the broader community response to his loss, as friends worked to help him navigate the aftermath of losing White while continuing to process the earlier loss of his son.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie moves forward with Midway Road expansion and Florida Turnpike interchange
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to FDOT for a partial interchange on the Turnpike. The $95 million Midway Road Widening Project is already underway.
cards.body:
Last month, the Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange on the Florida Turnpike. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said there is currently a significant gap between the entrances and exits to the Turnpike in Port St. Lucie. Samples said the interchange is about accessibility and keeping up with growth in the city over the next 20 to 50 years.

FDOT has been constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to help with congestion and safety. Crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes from Selvitz Road to Jenkins Road. The second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road is still in the design phase, with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. FDOT is also working on improving the Turnpike bridge and adding a partial interchange, which remains in the design phase. The Midway Road Widening Project will also add bike and pedestrian paths and sidewalks. City council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: West Palm Beach considers elevated self-driving transit connecting downtown to airport
cards.teaser: California-based Glydways will present a proposal to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday for an elevated network of autonomous vehicles connecting downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport.
cards.body:
Glydways, a California-based autonomous transit company, will present its elevated self-driving vehicle proposal to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday for initial consideration. The system would connect downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport, the convention center, Brightline and Tri-Rail stations. Small autonomous electric vehicles carrying four to six passengers would travel along a dedicated elevated guideway built above existing roads, potentially reducing the trip between downtown and the airport to less than 10 minutes. The company estimates seven minutes or less between the convention center and airport and roughly one to two minutes between Tri-Rail and the convention center. Senior Vice President Brian Gettinger said the concept functions like a "horizontal elevator," bypassing traffic entirely and making no intermediate stops.

Gettinger said West Palm Beach is uniquely positioned for the system because major transportation hubs already exist close together but are not easily connected for pedestrians or travelers. He cited increasing congestion along Okeechobee Boulevard, Southern Boulevard and Belvedere Road as evidence the region needs new transportation solutions. While Glydways has not disclosed a specific price, Gettinger said the system would cost "a small fraction" of traditional light rail, which previous South Florida discussions estimated at $400 million to $500 million per mile. Potential funding sources include Palm Beach County, the City of West Palm Beach, the Florida Department of Transportation, federal transit grants and public-private partnerships. Tuesday's meeting will determine whether the county should formally evaluate the proposal rather than approve construction.

City leaders announced the achievement at the National Civic League conference in Denver, where they presented Riviera Beach's approach to building community engagement.

Mayor Douglas Lawson expressed pride in the honor, calling Riviera Beach "one of the biggest, brightest, shining stars." He credited the award to the city's long-term revitalization efforts aimed at improving residents' quality of life. "They're seeing the changes; they're seeing the revitalization and the reimagining of Riviera Beach that we set out so many years to do," Lawson said. City leaders emphasize that the recognition reflects sustained work to strengthen civic health, build trust between residents and government, and give community members a genuine voice in shaping the city's future.

Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson attributed the award to residents themselves. "This award is a tribute to the heart and determination of our residents," Miller-Anderson said. "Every event we host, every project we complete, and every challenge we overcome happens because our community shows up for one another." She noted that the designation reinforces the city's positive momentum and community pride. According to city officials, the award demonstrates that collaboration drives results and shows the nation that residents remain deeply involved in directing their community's future.

The application showcased several civic programs, including the Riviera Beach Youth Council, which engages high school students in civic leadership and advocacy, the Citizens Leadership Academy with a 98 percent completion rate, and the Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program, which offers mini-grants for critical home repairs to longtime homeowners. Miller-Anderson emphasized the broader commitment behind these initiatives. "We're doing a lot of innovative things to make sure that our community is able to say that they are part of what's happening here in the city," she said. The All-America City Award, presented annually since 1949, ranks among the nation's most respected civic honors. City leaders say the designation celebrates progress and positions Riviera Beach for future opportunities and continued development. Other 2026 award winners include communities in Massachusetts, Tennessee, Texas, Alabama, North Carolina, Virginia, South Carolina, and Oregon.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie moves forward with Midway Road widening and Florida Turnpike interchange
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange on the Turnpike at Midway Road.
cards.body:
Last month, the Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange project on Florida's Turnpike. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said there is a significant gap between the entrances and exits to the Turnpike currently in the city. He said the interchange is designed to accommodate growth that has already occurred and growth expected over the next 20 to 50 years.

FDOT has been constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to help with congestion and safety. Crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes from Selvitz Road to Jenkins Road. The second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road is still in the design phase, with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. The partial interchange is also still in the design phase. FDOT said the project will add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks. City council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: Stuart downtown dock closes Monday for $3 million renovation, slip capacity nearly doubles
cards.teaser: Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a year-long $3 million renovation that will nearly double its capacity from 18 to 44 slips for motorized and.
cards.body:
Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a year-long $3 million renovation that will nearly double its capacity from 18 to 44 slips for motorized and non-motorized vessels. The project, funded by a state grant and transportation impact fees, is projected to be complete by next Fourth of July. The renovation will include a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock and a smaller floating platform. The dock currently serves more than 1,400 boaters annually. Stuart Mayor Sean Reed said the upgrades are designed to prevent storm damage during hurricanes and major storms.

During the closure, the city is working to accommodate businesses and boaters who rely on the dock. Tiki Taxi & Cruises, which operates off the dock, initially had concerns about continuing operations during construction. Austin Kuyrkendall, director of operations for Tiki Taxi & Cruises, said the city found a solution by allowing the company to build a gate at the end of the non-floating section of the downtown Stuart dock for boarding passengers. Boat captain Parker Fisher, who is based in Stuart, said the dock has needed work over the years and welcomed the investment in more floating docks.

cards.headline: West Palm Beach autonomous elevated transit system proposed to connect downtown to airport
cards.teaser: California-based Glydways is proposing an elevated network of self-driving vehicles that would connect downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport, with the trip potentially taking less than 10 minutes.
cards.body:
Glydways, a California-based autonomous transit company, will present its proposal to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday for initial consideration. The system would connect President Donald J. Trump International Airport to the convention center and nearby Brightline and Tri-Rail stations using small autonomous electric vehicles carrying four to six passengers along a dedicated elevated guideway built above existing roads. Senior Vice President Brian Gettinger said the system would function like a "horizontal elevator," with estimated travel times of seven minutes or less between the convention center and airport and roughly one to two minutes between Tri-Rail and the convention center. Gettinger noted that West Palm Beach is uniquely positioned for the system because major transportation hubs already exist close together but are not easily connected for pedestrians or travelers.

The company said the system would cost "a small fraction" of a traditional light rail system while offering comparable passenger capacity, referencing previous South Florida light rail discussions that carried estimates of $400 million to $500 million per mile. Potential funding sources include Palm Beach County, the City of West Palm Beach, the Florida Department of Transportation, federal transit grants and public-private partnerships. Gettinger emphasized that the service would be priced like public transit rather than private rideshare. Tuesday's County Commission meeting is expected to determine whether the county should formally evaluate the proposal, with a planning and design contract potentially awarded later this year.

cards.headline: Delray Beach golf training center Tee Box opening July 17 after $90,000 contractor setback
cards.teaser: Tom Molen's Tee Box, a new virtual golf training and performance center near Delray Beach along Jog Road south of Linton Boulevard, will open July 17 after a three-month delay caused by contractor problems.
cards.body:
Tom Molen, owner of Tee Box, a virtual golf training and performance center near Delray Beach along Jog Road south of Linton Boulevard, faced a three-month delay after problems with his licensed contractor. The work ultimately had to be redone, costing Molen approximately $90,000. This estimate does not include revenue lost during the delays or expenses for bringing in another contractor to complete the repairs. "It was double pay on a lot of things from electricians to HVAC to drywall," Molen said.

David Allan, founder of Code Pro of the Palm Beaches, said contractor-related issues are impacting a significant number of people across Palm Beach County, with an estimated 25% to 35% of homeowners and property owners facing major issues with unvetted contractors. Allan recommends using Palm Beach County's online portal to verify whether contractors have proper licenses and insurance before work begins. The most common contractor complaints in Palm Beach County involve roofing, windows, and air conditioning work. Despite the setbacks, Molen said he is moving forward with the grand opening for Tee Box set for July 17.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound woman dies in Monday house fire as community raises funds for fiance
cards.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside the couple's Hobe Sound home. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause.
cards.body:
A Hobe Sound man is leaning on his community after losing his fiancée in a deadly house fire earlier this week. Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside the couple's home. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause. The fire remains under investigation. Friends have since launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings.

Nina Fenn, a friend of White's for eight years, spoke about the loss. "It's just a terrible shame and awful loss of life," Fenn said. She learned of the death through a phone call from Mark. Fenn reflected on White as a Christian woman who loved gardening, plants and playing the piano, and was always the first to lend a hand. The loss is compounded by grief Mark has already endured. Mark lost his one and only child, Jacob, tragically. White's death adds another layer of heartbreak, as her birthday is July 4 and she passed just a few days before her birthday. Fenn said White's memory will live on in the hearts of those who loved her.

cards.headline: Lantana veteran gets roof fixed, lien removed after WPTV steps in
cards.teaser: Stephen McCoy, a disabled and retired veteran in Lantana, had a nearly $7,000 lien removed from his home and his roof repairs completed after WPTV contacted the contractor.
cards.body:
Stephen McCoy, a disabled and retired veteran from Lantana, hired Seabreeze Roofing and Sheet Metal in Boynton Beach to replace his nearly 20-year-old roof before hurricane season. He made six payments totaling more than $17,000 to the company but said they left two holes unfinished on the back of his home. After the work stalled, McCoy said the company stopped responding to his calls, texts and emails despite his repeated attempts to contact them between January 10 and February 5.

McCoy's situation worsened when Gulfeagle Supply filed a nearly $7,000 lien against his home, claiming Seabreeze Roofing failed to pay for materials supplied to McCoy's property. Worried about legal costs, McCoy turned to WPTV's Let's Hear It event. After investigative reporter Kate Hussey spoke directly with the owner of Seabreeze Roofing, a final waiver of lien signed by Gulfeagle Supply and notarized was delivered within an hour, lifting the lien from McCoy's home. The contractor also agreed to send crews back to finish the two problem areas on his roof, completing the work about an hour after McCoy received the waiver.

hero.headline: Saint Andrew's Scots football targets state title after 10-2 season and district championship
hero.body:
The Saint Andrew's Scots football program is working hard this summer with a clear goal: winning a state championship during the 2026 fall season. Last year, the team finished with a 10-2 record and claimed a district title, but a second-round playoff loss has motivated the players and coaching staff to push further this year. Head football coach Jimmy Robertson believes the senior class has the experience and drive to make this the best season in program history.

Robertson noted that most of the current seniors have been with the program for four years, with many joining through the middle school feeder program. Because they have experienced success throughout their careers, Robertson said "hopefully their senior year is the best season that we've had." With this veteran group leading the way, the program is confident it can take the next step toward a state title.

To prepare for a deeper playoff run, Saint Andrew's has intentionally scheduled tougher opponents this fall. Senior Jack Williams explained the reasoning behind this decision, saying the team wanted to compete against strong programs while also attracting new talent to the Scots. Senior Jack Whelche emphasized that the team's focus is purely on advancing further in the playoffs, noting that an undefeated regular season does not guarantee success if the team continues to exit in the second round. For Whelche, true improvement this season means going beyond last year's playoff performance.

The players are using summer workouts as daily motivation to build toward their ambitious goals. Senior Edmyer St. Jean said the training sessions give the team something to look forward to each day and help maintain focus on breaking their current record. As the Scots prepare for the 2026 season, the combination of experienced leadership, a challenging schedule, and dedicated summer preparation has the program positioned to make a serious run at the state title they are targeting.

cards.headline: Martin County maritime teams prepare for hundreds of Fourth of July boaters
cards.teaser: Martin County Maritime Response Unit will have two boats with medics on standby in the north and south parts of the county as hundreds of boaters celebrate the holiday weekend.
cards.body:
Hundreds of boaters are expected on Florida waterways this Fourth of July weekend. Lt. Brett Harry with Martin County Maritime Response Unit said his team is preparing for the holiday rush with two boats staffed with medics positioned in the north and south areas of Martin County.

Harry said the medics are ready to respond to any medical situation, from minor injuries like a stubbed toe to serious emergencies including cardiac events and potential spinal injuries. Boaters Brendan and Ashley Shannon, who launched from Sandsprit Park in Martin County on Friday with their young daughter and puppy, prioritize safety on the water. Harry urged all boaters to keep their eyes on the water, designate a driver and bring life vests, whistles and flotation devices. "Just have fun and be safe," Harry said about the holiday weekend.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board fights judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk comments
cards.teaser: The Martin County School Board filed court papers Thursday opposing an administrative law judge's recommendation to reinstate Matt Theobald, a Spectrum Academy teacher suspended after social media comments about Charlie Kirk.
cards.body:
Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009, was suspended last year after posting social media comments labeling Charlie Kirk as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi. Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone recommended Theobald be reinstated and awarded back pay and benefits. In a Thursday court filing, the Martin County School Board argued that Livingstone's findings "are not based upon competent substantial evidence" and claimed Theobald's Facebook post about Kirk was a "serious offense" that warranted removal.

According to an investigation report, Theobald admitted writing the comments but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page "within a discussion among personal acquaintances" and were not intended for public view. Livingstone cited a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling stating that disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds, on personal equipment, with no student involvement, violated the teacher's First Amendment rights. The school board retains final authority on whether Theobald will return to his position, with no timeline announced for a decision.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound community supports man who lost fiancé in deadly home fire
cards.teaser: Friends have launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild after a fire destroyed his and his fiancé Misty Dawn White's home in Hobe Sound earlier this week.
cards.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her Hobe Sound home she shared with her fiancé, Mark. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause, though the fire remains under investigation. The flames destroyed many of the couple's belongings, leaving the home in a state of devastation.

Nina Fenn, a friend of White's for eight years, learned of the death through a phone call from Mark. Friends have since launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild. Fenn described White as a Christian woman who loved gardening, plants, playing piano, kids and people, and was always the first to lend a hand. The loss is compounded by grief Mark has already endured after losing his only child, Jacob, tragically. White's birthday is July 4, just days after her death, adding another layer of heartbreak for those who knew her.

cards.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to receive 2026 All-America City Award
cards.teaser: Riviera Beach was one of 10 communities nationwide to receive the All-America City Award from the National Civic League, recognizing civic engagement and community collaboration.
cards.body:
The National Civic League announced Riviera Beach as one of 10 communities in the United States to receive the 2026 All-America City Award during a conference in Denver. Riviera Beach was the only Florida city selected for the honor this year. The award recognizes communities that bring residents, local government, businesses and organizations together to solve local challenges and create lasting change. Mayor Douglas Lawson called the recognition a proud moment for the city, saying "Little old Riviera Beach is one of the biggest, brightest, shining stars." Lawson said the city earned the award through a long-term effort to revitalize Riviera Beach and improve quality of life for residents.

Riviera Beach's application highlighted three specific programs: the Riviera Beach Youth Council, which helps high school students become involved in civic leadership and advocacy; the Citizens Leadership Academy, a civic education initiative with a 98 percent completion rate; and the Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program, which provides mini-grants to help longtime homeowners make critical repairs. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson said the award is a tribute to the heart and determination of residents and that winning the award reinforces the city's positive momentum. She noted that the designation positions the community for future opportunities and continued growth.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie moves forward with Midway Road expansion and Florida Turnpike interchange
cards.teaser: The Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance last month to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation for a partial interchange on the Turnpike.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie is moving forward with infrastructure improvements to address a significant gap between entrances and exits to Florida's Turnpike in the city. Last month, the Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said the interchange is designed to accommodate growth that has already occurred and growth expected over the next 20 to 50 years.

FDOT is constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to help with congestion and safety. Crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes from Selvitz Road to Jenkins Road. The second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road is still in the design phase, with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. FDOT is also improving the Turnpike bridge and adding a partial interchange, both still in the design phase. The project will also add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks. City council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: Lantana veteran gets lien removed and roof repaired after WPTV investigates roofing contractor
cards.teaser: Stephen McCoy, a disabled and retired veteran in Lantana, turned to WPTV after a roofing contractor left unfinished repairs and a nearly $7,000 lien on his home.
cards.body:
Stephen McCoy, a disabled and retired veteran from Lantana, hired Seabreeze Roofing and Sheet Metal in Boynton Beach to replace his nearly 20-year-old roof ahead of hurricane season. McCoy made six payments totaling more than $17,000 to the company but said they left two holes unfinished on the back of his home and stopped responding to his calls, texts and emails starting in January. After hearing back from a worker on Feb. 5 who promised the owner would call, McCoy said he never received contact from the company again.

McCoy's situation worsened when Gulfeagle Supply sent letters warning that it had filed a nearly $7,000 lien on his home. The lien document stated Gulfeagle Supply had furnished materials to Seabreeze Roofing for McCoy's property but was not paid for those supplies. After WPTV investigative reporter Kate Hussey spoke with the owner of Seabreeze Roofing, who declined to comment on camera citing legal reasons, the situation rapidly changed. Within an hour, Hussey returned to McCoy's home with a final waiver of lien signed by Gulfeagle Supply and notarized, lifting the lien from his property. About an hour after receiving the waiver, crews returned to finish the two problem areas on McCoy's roof.

hero.headline: Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach offers sea turtle nesting programs through September
hero.body:
Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach is offering educational and interactive programs during peak sea turtle nesting season through September. Guests can participate in guided Turtle Walks, the Hatchling Discovery Program, Hatchling Releases, Tidal Tots and Plastic Free July Community Action Day. The programs are designed to give visitors an opportunity to learn about sea turtle conservation along one of the world's busiest sea turtle nesting beaches.

The center's Turtle Walk program allows participants to observe the nesting process while learning about sea turtle biology, conservation and ongoing research efforts. Educational demonstrations may include the use of red-light headlamps, amber lighting, night scopes and research tag scanning equipment. Loggerhead Marinelife Center's education and research departments work together during nesting season to collect and analyze data related to nesting activity and hatchling success. Sea turtle nesting season in Florida typically runs from March through October. Conservation groups continue encouraging beachgoers to turn off beachfront lighting at night, properly dispose of trash and avoid disturbing nesting turtles or hatchlings. Registration information and program details are available through Loggerhead Marinelife Center.

cards.headline: North Palm Beach hosts Fourth of July fireworks and pool party at country club
cards.teaser: North Palm Beach residents and visitors will celebrate Independence Day with a full day of family-friendly activities, live entertainment and fireworks at North Palm Beach Country Club and The Clubhouse on July 4.
cards.body:
The free community event includes a pool party, lawn games, live music, a barbecue buffet and a fireworks finale scheduled for 9 p.m. Organizers say this years event also recognizes Americas 250th anniversary, bringing an added sense of celebration to the annual holiday tradition in Palm Beach County.

The festivities begin with a community pool party from 11 a.m. at the country club pool area. Guests can enjoy a water slide, DJ entertainment, games and activities, food and beverages and a poolside satellite bar. Beginning at 4:30 p.m., families can take part in activities including cornhole, Connect 4, giant Jenga, face painting and lawn games.

Live music from Solstice Reign is expected to begin around 6 p.m. Ashley Shipman, director of parks and recreation, said the golf course will offer one of the best locations to watch the fireworks display. The Clubhouse will also host a Fourth of July barbecue buffet from 4:30 p.m.

hero.headline: St. Petersburg selects $8.1 billion vision to redevelop Tropicana Field site
hero.teaser: Mayor Ken Welch chose a proposal led by Blake Investment Partners and Related Group to transform acres of stadium parking and public land into a mixed-use district with housing, hotels, cultural institutions and a 13-acre central park.
hero.body:
St. Petersburg Mayor Ken Welch has chosen The Burg Bid as the city's preferred proposal for transforming the Tropicana Field site and surrounding Historic Gas Plant District. The plan, led by Blake Investment Partners and Related Group, proposes an $8.1 billion mixed-use development that would replace the previous stadium-centered approach with a district organized around Samuel Davis Park, a 13-acre civic and cultural hub.

The development team would purchase 58 acres of city-owned land for $275 million, with the full land package valued at $405 million when including $130 million in land the city would retain. A $20 million deposit would be required when a purchase and sale agreement is finalized. Unlike earlier redevelopment plans centered on constructing a new baseball stadium, The Burg Bid proposal emphasizes cultural institutions and public space. Samuel Davis Park would anchor the district and include The Woodson African American Museum of Florida, a planned Museum of Public Art, a Discovery Center, event lawns, a playground, a splash pad, and a concert lawn. The park represents part of 18.5 acres of total public park space planned for the site. Blake Investment Partners CEO Thompson Whitney Blake described the project as resting "on respect for the community that once existed here, informing and educating the future generations."

The proposal emphasizes reconnecting with the Historic Gas Plant neighborhood, a predominantly Black community demolished decades ago for the stadium. The plan would preserve the original gas tank footprint within Samuel Davis Park and create a pedestrian corridor called the Legacy Link connecting City Hall with the Manhattan Casino and the Deuces District. Nine planned bridges over Booker Creek reference nine bridges that historically crossed the Gas Plant area, while restoration efforts would transform the creek from a drainage ditch back into a central natural feature with walking paths and community parks.

The development would deliver 3,600 income-restricted housing units over 15 years, with 1,800 units within the Historic Gas Plant District and 1,800 on complementary sites elsewhere in St. Petersburg. The plan includes homeownership opportunities at discounts to market value through partnership with affordable housing developer Blue Sky Communities. The project would be completed in three phases of approximately five years each, with early development beginning outside the stadium footprint before demolition. Phase 1 would establish cultural anchors and the Collaboratorium, a workforce training and small-business center. Phase 2 would develop mixed-income neighborhoods and strengthen connections to surrounding districts. Phase 3 would complete the project with a 4,000 to 5,000-seat Resilience Event Center, a Discovery Center, and a surf wave attraction. The team's lease with the city ends after the 2028 season.

cards.headline: DeSantis allies accuse Lieutenant Governor's wife of running anonymous accounts attacking Governor
cards.teaser: Multiple social media accounts were deactivated Friday after prominent veterans of Governor Ron DeSantis' communications team alleged the accounts were operated.
cards.body:
Multiple X accounts were deactivated after allegations from prominent veterans of Governor Ron DeSantis' communications team that they were operated by Layla Collins, wife of Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins. Christina Pushaw, a communications specialist in the Governor's Office, and Jeremy Redfern, Deputy Chief of Staff to Attorney General James Uthmeier, both pointed to online research tying the accounts to the Second Lady. Pushaw shared information from Promota CEO Robert Salvador showing that the account @FSUdude01670 appeared connected to a phone number and email similar to known contact information for Layla Collins. Florida Politics obtained screenshots verifying this through two-factor authentication, displaying an access attempt that triggered a message to a partially starred email address and a phone number with only the last digits visible.

Pushaw also identified a second account, @bobnamy1, that she said appeared tied to Layla Collins, stating its content consisted entirely of posts promoting Jay Collins and attacking people who did not endorse him, including the Governor. Redfern posted that the FSUDude account was tied directly to Layla Collins' personal cell phone number. Both accounts were deactivated after the public criticism. Florida Politics requested comments from Jay and Layla Collins. Both Pushaw and Redfern previously served as Press Secretaries for DeSantis. Redfern now works for Uthmeier, who has endorsed U.S. Representative Byron Donalds for Governor.

cards.headline: Secretary of State asks court to keep Republican candidate off ballot after filing disaster
cards.teaser: Secretary of State Cord Byrd is asking courts to keep Paula Stark off the ballot after she failed to properly submit required paperwork less than 30 minutes before the noon qualifying deadline on June 12.
cards.body:
Secretary of State Cord Byrd is asking Leon Circuit Court to keep St. Cloud Republican Paula Stark off the ballot, citing incomplete qualifying materials submitted less than 30 minutes before the noon deadline on June 12. Five state employees provided sworn declarations stating that Stark's treasurer and partner, Joel Davis, never submitted the required Form 6 nor received it back when submitting other paperwork. Byrd argued that Stark and Davis should have exercised care by questioning the missing Form 6 while Davis was at the Division office, or by submitting documents before the deadline rather than waiting until the final hour.

Three weeks after the qualifying deadline, Stark still has not submitted Form 6, a public disclosure of financial interests, according to Election Records Division Bureau Chief Erica Ikay Reeve. Stark was one of 12 candidates who improperly filed Form 6, though half of them corrected the problems and qualified. Reeve also cited Stark's history of campaign finance violations, including a report filed over one month late, excessive contributions, and an incorrect address on file. The state revoked Stark's Friends of Paula political committee in November over $16,000 in unpaid fines. If Stark is removed from the ballot, the House District 47 primary will feature only Democrats Jorge Figueroa and Anthony Nieves.

cards.headline: Beachgoer killed by lightning strike while swimming in Florida
cards.teaser: A person was killed by a lightning strike while swimming at a Florida beach. Witnesses described the sound as resembling an atomic bomb.
cards.body: A beachgoer was killed by a lightning strike while swimming in Florida on Friday. The New York Post reported that witnesses said the lightning strike sounded like an atomic bomb went off. The incident occurred as Fourth of July celebrations were beginning across the state.

cards.headline: New video shows aftermath of deadly alligator attack in Florida
cards.teaser: ABC News released new video showing the aftermath of a deadly alligator attack in Florida.
cards.body: New video has been released showing the aftermath of a deadly alligator attack that occurred in Florida. ABC News obtained and broadcast the footage on Friday. The video shows the scene following the fatal attack.

cards.headline: Lightning strike kills swimmer, injures three others as Fourth of July celebrations begin
cards.teaser: One person was killed and three others were injured by a lightning strike in Florida on Friday as Fourth of July celebrations were getting underway across the state.
cards.body: A lightning strike in Florida killed one person and injured three others on Friday as Fourth of July celebrations began. FOX Weather reported the incident occurred as holiday activities were starting across the state. The strike comes during a period of heightened outdoor activity for the Independence Day weekend.

cards.headline: District 21 Democratic candidates outline positions on utilities, housing and schools
cards.teaser: Democratic candidates running for District 21 are sharing their positions on Gainesville Regional Utilities, housing and schools in advance of the primary election.
cards.body: Democratic candidates competing for District 21 are discussing their positions on major local issues including Gainesville Regional Utilities, housing and schools. The Independent Florida Alligator reported Friday on what the candidates are saying about these key topics. The candidates are outlining their policy positions ahead of the upcoming primary election.

hero.headline: Hobe Sound woman dies in home fire days before her birthday
hero.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her home. Friends have launched a fundraiser to help her fiance Mark rebuild.
hero.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her home in Hobe Sound. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office suggest an electrical issue may have caused the fire, though the investigation remains ongoing. The blaze destroyed many of the belongings of White and her fiancé Mark, leaving the family facing significant loss.

Nina Fenn, who had been friends with White for eight years, learned of the tragedy through a phone call from Mark. Speaking about the incident, Fenn said, "It's just a terrible shame and awful loss of life." She visited the scene in the days following the fire to process her grief. Friends have since launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild after losing so much in the flames. "It's completely a state of devastation," Fenn said of the situation.

White's life was defined by her generosity and faith, according to those who knew her best. Fenn reflected on their friendship and how she wants White to be remembered, describing her as someone with a genuine love for others. "Misty was a Christian woman. She loved gardening and plants. She plays the piano. She was always the first to lend a hand. She loves kids; she loves her kids. She loves people," Fenn said. The loss hits especially hard for Mark, who has endured previous tragedy. Fenn explained that Mark lost his only child, Jacob, in a tragic incident. "Mark lost his one and only child, Jacob, and lost him tragically. So, I just am trying whatever I can to support him," Fenn said.

The timing of White's death adds another layer of heartbreak to an already devastating situation. Her birthday was coming up on the Fourth of July, meaning she passed away just days before turning 47. This cruel timing has weighed heavily on those who cared about her. Fenn expressed how White's memory will continue to live on in the hearts of those she touched. "She's always been a good soul to me. She'll always be in our hearts," Fenn said.

The board's attorney claims Theobald's Facebook post about Kirk was a serious offense and that removing him was appropriate. Livingstone cited a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling that said disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds, on personal equipment, with no student involvement, violated the teacher's First Amendment rights. According to an investigation report, Theobald admitted writing the comments about Kirk but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page within a discussion among personal acquaintances and were not intended for public view. The school board retains final authority on whether Theobald returns to his position.

hero.headline: Costco plans first Treasure Coast store in Port St. Lucie
hero.teaser: Costco is planning its first Treasure Coast location in Port St. Lucie.
hero.body:
Costco is planning to open its first Treasure Coast store in Port St. Lucie. The warehouse retailer has announced plans for the new location, marking a significant retail expansion for the region that includes Martin, St. Lucie, and Indian River counties. Port St. Lucie residents have not previously had access to a Costco warehouse in the immediate area, making this development an important addition to local shopping options.

The timing of this announcement comes as Port St. Lucie undergoes major infrastructure improvements to support continued growth. The city is actively working on a $95 million Midway Road Widening Project designed to address congestion and safety concerns. The first phase of construction is currently underway, expanding the road from two lanes to four lanes between Selvitz Road and Jenkins Road. The second phase, which will widen the road from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road, remains in the design phase with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027.

In addition to the Midway Road improvements, Port St. Lucie is working to enhance accessibility in the region. The city council approved the first reading of an ordinance to donate 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to support a partial interchange on Florida's Turnpike. According to Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, the interchange addresses a critical gap in current access points. "There's a pretty significant gap between the entrances and exits to the Turnpike currently in Port St. Lucie," Samples said. He emphasized that the project aims to accommodate growth that has already occurred and growth expected over the next 20 to 50 years. The partial Turnpike interchange remains in the design phase. The Midway Road Widening Project will also include bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks.

While construction activity has been noticeable for residents, local support for the improvements appears strong. Port St. Lucie resident Erin Scheumeister acknowledged the inconvenience of ongoing work but recognized its necessity. "We definitely needed it to be expanded," Scheumeister said. "It'll be a lot better and easier to get to work." The city council is expected to vote on final approval to donate the land at an upcoming meeting. These infrastructure investments position Port St. Lucie to better serve both current residents and future population growth while supporting new commercial development like the planned Costco location.

hero.headline: Indian River State College Promise Program helps students earn debt-free degrees
hero.body:
Indian River State College operates a Promise Program designed to help students achieve debt-free college degrees. The program removes financial barriers that prevent residents from pursuing higher education by providing support to cover the costs associated with attending the college. Through this initiative, students can complete their education and earn credentials without taking on student loan debt that typically accompanies a college degree.

The Promise Program represents a significant effort to expand access to higher education across the Treasure Coast region. Indian River State College serves students throughout multiple counties in the area, offering associate degrees and certificate programs to local residents seeking career training and academic advancement. By addressing the financial obstacles that can prevent students from enrolling or completing their studies, the program aims to make college more accessible to a broader population.

The college's commitment to debt-free education aligns with broader trends in Florida's focus on educational access and affordability. Many institutions across the state are exploring ways to support student success through innovative financing and support programs. Indian River State College's Promise Program reflects this commitment by helping students achieve their educational goals while minimizing financial burden.

Students who participate in the Promise Program graduate with the knowledge and credentials needed for career advancement in their chosen fields, but without the weight of substantial student debt. This approach recognizes that financial barriers often prevent capable students from completing their degrees and entering the workforce. By removing this obstacle, the college helps more students from the community realize their educational aspirations and contribute to the region's economic development.

cards.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs up 4 percent this year
cards.teaser: Holiday meals for Independence Day celebrations cost more in 2026 than last year, according to a national survey.
cards.body:
A Fourth of July cookout for 10 people now costs $73.82, up 4 percent from a year ago, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey. The price increases are driven by inflation across multiple traditional holiday foods. Ground beef prices rose 5.5 percent and buns increased 7.7 percent. Strawberries saw the largest price jump at 12.4 percent following a Florida frost that damaged crops. Ice cream prices also climbed 5.3 percent.

Not all items have increased in cost. Potato prices are down this year, offering savings for those planning potato dishes. Corn prices have fluctuated, though locally grown corn from the Glades can provide the best deals. Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch recommends shoppers compare stores to find the best deals for groceries on their lists. She emphasized that cutting down food waste through meal planning is the biggest thing families can do to control costs during the holiday season.

cards.headline: Breast cancer patient denied insurance coverage hours before reconstruction surgery
cards.teaser: Beth Clark and her surgeon are speaking out after Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield denied coverage for a reconstruction procedure less than 24 hours before it was scheduled.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma three months ago and underwent a full double bilateral mastectomy. Less than 24 hours before her scheduled reconstruction surgery, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield denied coverage for the procedure involving GalaFlex surgical mesh. According to the denial letter, the surgery is still considered "investigational" and "there is no or not enough proof it improves health." GalaFlex is a synthetic surgical mesh approved by the FDA for some uses in the body but not for breast reconstruction. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA stated its "efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined."

Dr. Alicia Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, uses GalaFlex mesh on most of her breast reconstruction patients and says the product gives her patients the least amount of complications compared to other options. "This product is giving my patients the least amount of complications, and other plastic surgeons as well," Billington said. Despite Anthem's denial, Clark received her reconstruction surgery with the GalaFlex mesh a little more than a week ago through arrangements made by Billington. Last year, Cigna became the first and only major insurer to start approving GalaFlex for breast reconstruction. Clark and Billington are continuing to fight the denial, while a new bill has been introduced to modernize the Women's Health and Cancer Rights Act.
